sections.heading: 1. Using springs in rehab
lines: ① Learn the move lying down, springs assisting.
② Change one spring at a time to add load.
③ Return the carriage slowly, over 3 seconds.
④ Progress to standing work when ready.

sections.heading: 2. Stop and tell us if…
lines: Pain keeps building during a move, or

caption:
Momo has been resting a sore knee, and the reformer springs looked a bit scary at first.

Here's why they're handy in rehab. Springs can resist a movement or assist it, so early on you can practise a squat or leg press with support, then gradually take that support away. Each spring change shifts the load in a small, predictable step.

Many exercises are done lying or seated, so you can train legs, hips and trunk without full bodyweight through a sore knee. And controlling the carriage on the way back builds strength through the whole range.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with an assessment and adjusts things as you progress. Book online via the link in bio.
